memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Vitamin B12 deficiency, depression, and hypothyroidism.
Evidence: Serum B12 140 pg/mL (low), MCV 104 fL (high), Hb 10.8 g/dL (low); PHQ-9 16 (moderate depression); TSH 9.0 mIU/L (high), free T4 0.7 ng/dL (low).
Symptoms and examination: Fatigue, paresthesias in feet, low mood, weight gain, cold intolerance, dry skin; pulse regular, lungs clear, thyroid not enlarged.
Plan: Start methylcobalamin 1500 mcg OD, sertraline 50 mg OD, levothyroxine 50 mcg OD. Smoking status: never. Inhaler technique not applicable. Review in 8 weeks.

Vitamin B12 deficiency improving, hypothyroidism partially treated, depression moderate.
Evidence: B12 now 300 pg/mL, MCV 98 fL, Hb 12.5 g/dL; TSH 5.2 mIU/L, free T4 0.9 ng/dL; PHQ-9 10.
Symptoms and examination: Less fatigue, mood better, occasional cold intolerance, mild weight gain; lungs clear, no thyroid enlargement.
Plan: Continue methylcobalamin, increase levothyroxine to 100 mcg OD, increase sertraline to 100 mg OD. Smoking status: never. Inhaler technique not applicable. Review in 8 weeks.
